formative_worksheets.title: Tables and Operations Check
formative_worksheets.when_to_use: After Lesson 3, before Lesson 4. Quick mid-unit check (15 minutes) to confirm C1.1 (operations), C1.2 (table of values), and C1.3 (multi-step rules) have landed before adding formal far-prediction and justification in Lesson 4.
formative_worksheets.purpose: Standalone formative assessment distinct from lesson worksheets. Lets the teacher quickly see which children can identify operations, build tables of values, AND extend a multi-step rule, and which need a bridging conversation before Lesson 4's most demanding work.
formative_worksheets.student_learning_goal: I can name the operation and the rule of a pattern AND build a table of values for it.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can name the operation and the rule of a pattern AND build a table of values for it.
header.character_watermark: Coco the Conductor in the top-right corner with a small magnifying glass — the 'check-in' Coco. Small (~1.5in tall). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

prompts.prompt: Look at each pattern. Write the operation and the rule on the lines.
prompts.visual_layout: Three pattern strips stacked vertically. Strip A: 4-cell number row 5, 10, 15, 20 (rule +5, additive). Strip B: 4-cell number row 1, 3, 9, 27 (rule ×3, multiplicative). Strip C: 5-cell number row 10, 14, 12, 16, 14 (rule +4 then -2, compound). Beside each, two writing lines: 'Operation: ___. Rule: ___.'

image_placeholders.description: A 4-cell horizontal number-row strip in B&W line-art with the digits 5, 10, 15, 20 — a +5 additive growing pattern. Footprints beneath. Labelled 'A' to the left.
A 4-cell horizontal number-row strip with the digits 1, 3, 9, 27 — a ×3 multiplicative growing pattern. Footprints beneath. Labelled 'B' to the left.
A 5-cell horizontal number-row strip with the digits 10, 14, 12, 16, 14 — a multi-step +4 then -2 pattern. Footprints beneath. Labelled 'C' to the left.

prompts.answer_key: A: Operation=ADDITION. Rule=+5. B: Operation=MULTIPLICATION. Rule=×3. C: Operation=multi-step (addition + subtraction). Rule=+4 then -2.

prompts.prompt: Build a table of values for this growing pattern. Then predict term 10.
prompts.visual_layout: Top: a pre-built 4-cell number sequence 7, 14, 21, 28 (rule +7). Below: an empty 2-column table with TERM and VALUE headers, 5 data rows, term column pre-filled 1-5. Below the table: 'Rule: +____.' and 'Term 10 = ____'.

image_placeholders.description: A 4-cell horizontal number-row strip in B&W line-art with the digits 7, 14, 21, 28 — a +7 additive growing pattern. Footprints beneath. Full width.
A 2-column table of values, ~3in wide × 3in tall. 6 rows (1 header + 5 data). Headers TERM and VALUE in bold uppercase. Term column pre-filled 1-5. Value column empty. Thin black borders.

prompts.answer_key: Value column: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35. Rule = +7. Term 10 = 70 (since values are term × 7).

prompts.prompt: How are you feeling about operations, multi-step rules, and tables of values? Circle the face that fits.
prompts.visual_layout: Three faces in a horizontal row: smile, neutral, frown. Below each: 'I got it!', 'Almost!', 'Need help!'.

image_placeholders.description: Three round face icons in a horizontal row, each ~1.5in across. Left face: smiling. Middle: neutral. Right: downturned. Labels beneath: 'I got it!', 'Almost!', 'Need help!'. Total row width ~6in. B&W line art.

prompts.answer_key: Open. Use alongside Prompts 1 and 2 to identify mismatches: a child who got Prompt 1 wrong but circled 'I got it!' may need more discussion; a child who got Prompts 1 and 2 right but circled 'Need help!' may just need confidence-building.

formative_worksheets.teacher_notes: Administer between Lesson 3 and Lesson 4 — the 15-minute mid-unit gate. Score guide: 2/2 + correct table headers + multi-step rule named correctly + confident self-rating = ready for Lesson 4. 1/2 + correct table = brief 1:1 conference reviewing the multi-step rule notation. Children who left the value column blank or wrote the term number in the value column need a re-loop on the table-of-values structure. Children who got the multi-step rule on Prompt 1.C without prompting are at L3+ on C1.3.

reflection_sheet.title: My Pattern Parade Reflection
reflection_sheet.purpose: End-of-unit metacognition. Children look back at their week of pattern work — including the new Grade 3 expectations of operations, multi-step rules, tables of values, far prediction, and formal justification — and rate themselves, name a favourite, name a struggle, and set a forward goal.
reflection_sheet.student_learning_goal: I can think about what I learned this week.

reflection_sheet.teacher_notes: Hand out at the very end of Lesson 5, alongside the Junior Pattern Conductor certificate ceremony. Grade 3 children can write multi-sentence responses to prompts 3-5 — encourage but accept invented spelling. Prompt 2 explicitly maps to all Grade 3 expectations including the new ones (multi-step rules, far prediction, justification, numbers to 1000) so a NO on any line tells you what to revisit. Read responses to inform unit notes for next year. The yes/no audit on Prompt 2 is also a quick teacher check: a 'NO' on 'I justified my prediction' even from a child who clearly did this aloud may signal that the SENTENCE FRAME wasn't internalized — worth a 30-second conference.
